top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is an original invention: the magic-wavelength condition equalises the light shift for both clock states, so many atoms can be held free of Doppler and recoil shifts, which is what made 10^-18 reachable. It is experimentally verified across independent laboratories and already gives a new measurement window (millimetre-scale gravitational redshift). The two-name credit to Katori (proposal and first strontium demonstrations) and Ye (frontier accuracy and stability) is compact and defensible, with the citation kept on the invention and verified performance rather than on unobserved fundamental-physics claims. The residual risks (priority claims of Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Derevianko and others, and distinctness from combs and ion clocks) should be confirmed by expert reports, but they do not outweigh the case for awarding over no award.
